I think the complaints of people who are unhappy about EIP-8037 breaking a few contracts are valid and very reasonable.

We do NOT want an Ethereum where it becomes "prudent security advice" to have centralized upgrade hatches "just in case".

I do think that on-net 8037, and a couple of other large breaking changes coming up, are necessary to get Ethereum to a healthy long-term stable state. But it should not be *easy* to make such deep changes to Ethereum. A social norm that, at the very least, core devs have a responsibility to support any app that breaks because a fork broke some aspect of Ethereum that the devs justifiably thought was rock solid is very good to have.

To that end I'm glad that people in @ethereumfndn, @ethlabs_org and elsewhere have been working hard to help app devs with upgrades. Such efforts should continue and increase. Given its breaking nature, Glamsterdam should not be rushed.

I also hope everyone on all sides stays engaged for similar conversations around the next few forks.

The majority of Rockstar employees in the UK have voted against union recognition following GTA 6’s record-breaking launch.

One employee explained why:

“A recognized union has real and complicated consequences on how a workplace operates, which are legally binding. It's not just some fantastic rainbow of workers' rights. It's a fundamental change to how the workplace is structured and how people's individual contributions and career progression is handled.

Also, for what it's worth: Rockstar did not coerce my vote whatsoever, and the vote was 100% anonymous and handled by an independent third-party.”

Rockstar’s head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe stated that the result reflects the team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make the company so innovative and strong.
